title: Borrow UInt64Buffer in exact kernels
objective: Allow otherwise exact IntegerBuffer kernels to borrow UInt64Buffer len/get/set with preserved uint64 typing, checked bounds and isolated same-source native lowering

handoff.summary: General exact-kernel IR now borrows UInt64Buffer values for checked len/get/set while preserving uint64 data and mutation effects. Exact Integer modulo uint64 lowers to a host-isolated limb-native operation. The actual Round-4 batch and its evolved two-level CRT ABI both compile with zero callbacks; randomized JavaScript, tagged, GMP, native, and CPython differentials pass.
risks: The coordinator intentionally stopped the redundant lane-local full native sweep after it passed build, FLINT, FFLAS, graph, M4RI, FFI/lifecycle, canonical native-kernel, and dense migration stages; the authoritative final native sweep runs on the integrated root.
next_steps: Use the integrated root native/platform sweep as the release receipt.
Retain the registered exact word-buffer witness in the integration tier.
